source.title: Data curation via joint example selection further accelerates multimodal learning
source.authors: Talfan Evans; Nikhil Parthasarathy; Hamza Merzic; Olivier J. Hénaff

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance in multimodal contrastive pretraining, a different modality and training setting from the language-model loss scaling claim.
record.gate_note: The study does not fit power laws to held-out pretraining loss or test loss extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or architecture-shape effects. Its relevant results are downstream task scores across training-example budgets; batch-selection and FLOP-efficiency results do not by themselves test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a data-curation method paper (JEST). It reports its own method's downstream scores and efficiency against uniform and prior baselines. It fits no power law to loss, compute, parameters or data and makes no predictive analysis. 'Neural scaling laws' appears only as framing: curation as 'a new dimension for neural scaling laws'. Downstream scores rising with more training examples within one method are a performance comparison, not a test of whether downstream performance scales predictably.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Jointly selecting learnable batches, steered by reference models trained on small curated data, accelerates multimodal contrastive pretraining. It matches or exceeds SOTA with up to 13x fewer iterations and 10x less compute.
record.recipe_differences: Multimodal image-text contrastive pretraining with joint data selection; evaluates downstream task performance and training efficiency rather than fitting language-model held-out loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with filtering ratio, reference dataset and model, training-example budget, and whether approximate scoring/multi-resolution training is used.

fits_no_version.finding: Online joint batch selection with a curated reference model reaches a uniform baseline's downstream performance with up to 13x fewer examples and about 10x fewer FLOPs. JEST gains track reference-model training up to about 1B reference examples, then saturate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data curation level shifts the downstream performance-vs-compute curve of contrastive image-text pretraining (curation as a scaling dimension).

record.problems: No held-out pretraining-loss measurements or scaling-law fits; downstream curves are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates or a formal predictive analysis.
record.rows_left_out: Other downstream benchmark values in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 5 are not separately recorded: they compare methods, datasets, or reference models without adding a training-scale progression relevant to V6. Figure-only numerical curve values are not extracted.

untested.parts: No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Multimodal training, but no power-law form is tested on loss or performance.
No test of predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss. Only method comparisons are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped: the rows are the study's own method against baselines. The Table 4 rows also mix up JEST/Flexi-JEST subjects and budgets (5B is JEST, 13B is Flexi-JEST).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep over parameter count and token count to find a compute-optimal allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The study uses multimodal training but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for pretraining loss in another modality or training regime.
No downstream prediction from pretraining loss or fitted predictive law; measurements concern multimodal downstream scores over selected training budgets.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices or setups.
